editorial:
You meet Vivo, a tiny kinkajou with a big heart and an even bigger love for music. He lives happily with his owner Andrés in Havana, where they perform together in the plaza. When Andrés gets a letter from his old friend Marta, a famous singer, he plans to travel to Miami to deliver a love song he wrote for her years ago. But tragedy strikes before he can make the trip. Determined to honor his friend, Vivo sets off on a wild journey to deliver that song himself. Along the way he meets Gabi, a loud and lovable girl who becomes his unlikely partner. The movie bursts with color, catchy songs, and warm humor that pulls you right in.

The animation is gorgeous, and the music keeps your toes tapping. Lin-Manuel Miranda's songs are a real highlight. The pacing moves quickly, though some side characters feel a little thin. Still, the heart of the film shines through. Families, music lovers, and animation fans will all find something to enjoy.
endingExplained: Vivo finally reaches Miami and makes it to Marta's farewell concert. He gets the song to her just in time, and she performs it on stage, finally hearing the love Andrés carried for her all those years. The crowd is moved, and Marta is deeply touched. Afterward, Vivo decides to stay with Gabi and her mother, finding a new family. The film closes on a joyful note, with music bringing everyone together and Andrés's memory honored through the song he never got to deliver himself.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves animated musicals and family adventures.
